heading: Records and caches in the browser
body:
A browser Store keeps records, such as a list of products, in IndexedDB. IndexedDB is a database that is built into the browser. Mark the record type with `Entity` and `Table`, and mark the class that saves and finds records with `Store`. When the Entity names the adapter "indexeddb", you write no adapter code. This works in JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart and Ruby services, and in Go, Rust and C# services that run as WebAssembly. Tachyon keeps one IndexedDB object store for each Table. The data never leaves the browser.

A cache keeps the answer of a method, so the next call with the same arguments does not run the method again. Mark the method with `Cached`, and name its cache with `CacheSettings`. In the browser, Tachyon keeps the cache in the Cache API, the storage for answers that is built into the browser. The cache has limits: ttlMs (how long an answer stays), maxBytes (the size of one answer) and maxEntries (the number of answers).

For complete examples in every language, read Data access: Tac and Caching: Tac on the Annotations A–Z page. Never save secrets in the browser.
